mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1000.0 for two consecutive months indicates robust consumer demand and construction activity, which historically produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to improved economic momentum and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return distribution shows negative returns in more than 50% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1000.0 for two consecutive months, or the rank correlation coefficient falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) decline below 0.15% for at least one month signals aggressive monetary easing that reduces risk-free rates and compresses equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.15%, or the average return in such periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in employment (PAYEMS) and industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 0.1% in one month indicate robust economic expansion that accelerates corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and INDPRO both > 0.1% change in 1 month
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when both PAYEMS and INDPRO rise by >0.1% in one month, or the rank correlation coefficient is negative.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic regimes, rising housing starts (HOUST) above 1000.0 signals continued consumer confidence and construction momentum that supports positive equity returns over the next 5 trading days, but this effect weakens in early-cycle conditions.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when HOUST rises in late-cycle expansion, or the effect is not distinguishable from baseline returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 235.0 for two consecutive months indicates persistent inflationary pressure that triggers central bank tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 235.0 for two consecutive months, or the rank correlation coefficient falls below -0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) decline below 5.0% for at least one month signals a tight labor market that fuels wage growth and corporate profit margins, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is below 5.0%, or the average return in such periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 0.5% and a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) decline below 0.15% in one month indicates strong consumer demand coupled with accommodative monetary policy, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when HOUST rises by >0.5% and FEDFUNDS is below 0.15%, or the rank correlation coefficient is negative.

mechanism_narrative: In supply-constrained economic regimes, a rising industrial production index (INDPRO) above 105.0 for two consecutive months signals increasing output capacity that supports positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days, but this effect is muted in supply-abundant conditions.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO rises in a supply-constrained regime, or the effect is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).
